Had this thought just before which I think is probably true. I'm no longer on facebook, but when I was, I noticed that any girl (and some guys) who posted a photo got a whole bucket of likes and comments saying stuff like "wow girl, looking good!!!".

Sometimes they were looking good, but more often than not they were not. Either fat, or just a shit photo, often both.

I think the constant praise, even when it's not deserved, is actually harmful and promotes this "body positive" bullshit. If you're always called beautiful, why improve? If we actually told people they looked like shit, perhaps they'd work on improving themselves.

What do you think?
Do you think facebook has made the fat problem worse? I do.
Social media is all about validation. You can tell the insecure ones by the frequency of their selfies.

I don't think it's really Facebook at all; this crap was all over MySpace, as well (I never used anything before MS but I'm sure it existed then too). Rather all those bullshit likes and comments are just a natural extension of undeserved praise and political correctness that you see everywhere in person. Everyone is so afraid of getting their feefees hurt that telling the truth, even in a polite and constructive manner, is a quick way to get yourself vilified. Objectivity was thrown out the window and now all that's left is the echo chamber.

Social media doesn't work the way you think it would. For girls it's something like - 10/10 hot, you get some likes but no comments or joke comments; above average hot, maybe a few people comment you look good; average, a bunch of dudes try to hit on you and you get some girls saying you look good; borderline, desperate betas show up in droves and girls are like aww she has to be uglier than me, I better say something nice; dumpster fire, multiply borderline by 10.

10/10 hot, you get some likes but no comments or joke comments

Everyone knows they look good, so nobody wants to be 'that guy' who hits on hot girls on Facebook. If they're super fat/ugly, people always compliment them because apparently being ugly and posting pictures of yourself on the internet is now enough to qualify as brave.
Facebook certainly aids in the spread of fat acceptance propaganda!

If facebook has contributed in any unique way, I would say it's via their growing policy of removing weight loss before and after pics, citing them as problematic and potentially offensive. If someone's chronicled positive achievement toward health and improving their appearance "triggers" you that much, then you need to seriously remove yourself from social media.

I see issues with the censorship of social media sites, usually biased towards fat chicks who can get away with more sexual content (nudity) on facebook and instagram than girls with hot bodies, who have their non rule breaking pics or their accounts removed for no good reason.

The fat chicks are more likely to mass report something benign for rule breaking than the fit/ skinny women are for nude hams. The amount of complaints (on all social media) seems to have more of an effect than any actual rule breaking.

I don't think it's Facebook in particular. Social media is just a conduit through with shitty, vapid people can exchange hollow flattery. You see it anywhere people talk to each other. It's a problem with society that we must compliment fat people because reasons.

The Internet has made ALL deviant behaviors 'worse.' Pre-Internet, when there was only one person in town into [stupid fringe hobby or idea] that shit got shut down quick. Now people can seek out other people and start the vicious retard cycle of reassurance that spawned furries and HAES.

As soon as the outcasts started posting their diaries online and calling them 'blogs' shit changed.

Facebook makes EVERYTHING worse, not just the fat problem. It distils human interaction into the most shallow and narcissistic form possible.

Delete your profile, and get on with living your life.
